overview: FAM4301 is a flight event focused on obogs and pressurization system. The notes below are organized off the canonical syllabus items first, then filled out with local FAM gouge so students can brief the event, explain the why behind each item, and stay ahead of instructor follow-up questions.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

children.text: The pressurization system regulates cockpit pressure during flight to maintain pilot comfort and safety. It uses engine bleed air and a system of valves and regulators to maintain a cockpit pressure altitude of 8,000 ft until a delta P (differential pressure) of 3.6 ± 0.2 psi is reached. Maximum cockpit pressure altitude at service ceiling (31,000 ft) is ~16,600 ft.
Routes high-temp engine bleed air to ECS subsystems.
Conditioned bleed air is tapped from the engine and routed to the OBOGS concentrator.
Uses pressure swing adsorption and a molecular sieve to extract oxygen from bleed air and remove nitrogen.
A small tank downstream of the concentrator that holds a short-term oxygen supply in the event of OBOGS failure.

The On-Board Oxygen Generating System (OBOGS) provides each T-6B pilot with an unlimited-duration, automatically regulated oxygen supply using filtered engine bleed air. It generates breathable oxygen using a molecular sieve and delivers it through cockpit-mounted oxygen regulators. In case of OBOGS failure, backup oxygen is available via the ejection seat emergency oxygen system.
OBOGS FAIL should illuminate within 20–30 sec if successful, and extinguish within 2 min once oxygen level recovers.
4-minute warm-up after activation before OBOGS FAIL annunciator is functional.
